title: Constipation Treatment Comparison in Children With Autism and Functional Constipation (CLEAR)
official: Constipation Liberation: Evaluating Agents for Response in Children With Autism
summary: This study is a multicenter, prospective, randomized, open-label, pragmatic trial comparing linaclotide with polyethylene glycol 3350 (PEG-3350) for treatment of functional constipation in autistic children aged 2 to 17 years. Approximately 320 participants will be randomized 1:1 to receive one of the two approved treatments and followed for 12 weeks. The primary hypothesis is that linaclotide will be more effective than PEG-3350 as first-line therapy.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria

* Male or female children aged 2 to 17 years at the time of consent.
* Diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) made by a qualified healthcare provider.
* Diagnosis of functional constipation meeting Rome IV criteria for at least 1 month prior to enrollment.
* Relatively treatment-naive to both study interventions within the previous 6 months.
* Parent(s)/legal guardian(s) willing and able to provide informed consent.
* Participant and caregiver willing and able to comply with protocol-required procedures.

Exclusion Criteria

* Constipation attributable to an organic or structural gastrointestinal disorder.
* Previous bowel surgery.
* Significant chronic gastrointestinal disorder.
* Significant systemic medical condition.
* Known pregnancy.
* Greater than one previous admission for bowel clean out.
* Refusal or allergy to taking either PEG-3350 or linaclotide.
